mcat_description.short: Prefabricated metal houses are factory-fabricated, knock-down or modular residential and accommodation structures built on mild steel (MS) or galvanised iron (GI) frames with insulated metal panel cladding, assembled on-site with minimal civil work. They are sold as complete turnkey units or as component kits, quoted per square foot.
mcat_description.long: Prefabricated metal houses are engineered building structures where all structural components — MS or GI frames, wall panels, roof panels, doors, and windows — are manufactured in a factory and assembled at the site, enabling rapid deployment compared to conventional brick-and-mortar construction. The primary construction systems used in India include MS tube/section frames with GI sheet or PUF sandwich panel cladding, Light Gauge Steel Framing (LGSF) with cement-fibre or GI board infill, and modular box units on steel chassis. These structures serve residential accommodation, labour camps, site offices, portable clinics, and institutional housing needs across India, with customisation in floor area, number of storeys, insulation grade, and internal fittings. Structural steel used in these houses is governed by IS 2062 (hot-rolled structural steel) and IS 1786 (TMT reinforcement bars), while the overall building must comply with local municipal bylaws and the National Building Code.

market_context: Prefabricated metal houses in India are commercially dominated by MS (mild steel) and GI (galvanised iron) frame-and-panel systems, with PUF sandwich panels increasingly adopted for insulation performance. The Indian prefab buildings market is projected to reach USD 15 billion in 2025 growing at ~8.8% CAGR to USD 23 billion by 2030, driven by PMAY affordable housing, smart city initiatives, and infrastructure project accommodation demand. Modular buildings hold the largest product-type share (~40%) in 2024, with panelised and componentised systems growing fastest at ~9.6% CAGR. Key Indian manufacturers include Tata Steel Nest-In (MobiNest), EPACK Prefab, Everest Industries, Interarch Building Products, PEBS Pennar, and Kirby Building Systems India. Structural steel used in these houses must comply with IS 2062 (hot-rolled structural steel) and IS 1786 (TMT bars); the finished structure must conform to local municipal bylaws and the National Building Code. Buyer vocabulary in India strongly favours 'readymade house', 'readymade ghar', and 'portable ghar' over technical terms, with 'tin makan' used in rural/semi-urban segments for basic GI sheet structures. Units are quoted per sq ft of built-up area across all commercial segments. Government procurement (PMAY-U, disaster relief, smart city) is a significant demand driver alongside private contractor and individual buyer segments.
